brief:
Guggenheim reports the S&P 500 fell into a technical correction, a 10 percent pullback from its high, after a seventh straight losing session. The Dow fell 8.0 percent, the S&P 500 8.6 percent, and the Nasdaq 10.0 percent for the week, with technology weakest. Strong Nvidia results and Anthropic's IPO failed to revive AI-trade optimism, and the selloff was global, worsened by Iran-strike and hack/outage risk.

Fed commentary leaned hawkish. Waller, citing broadening inflation and fear that 3 percent becomes the new norm, wants a 50 basis point December hike unless the Fed signals a faster pace. Jefferson, Goolsbee, and Kashkari each tied the AI buildout to inflation, overheating, or concentration risk, with Goolsbee open to a larger hike and Musalem backing multiple increases. Williams wants more progress toward 2 percent but rejects an outsized move. FOMC minutes show nearly all officials expect further hikes, two open to more than 25 basis points in December.

Separately, Q3 S&P 500 earnings are running strong, 84 percent beating estimates and up 32 percent year over year versus a 25 percent prior estimate, with full-year growth seen moderating into 2028. Jobless claims ticked up above consensus and October retail sales growth moderated.
